title: Inorganic carbon and phosphate beyond water-mass mixing on the Pearl River adjacent shelf
judge: Codex, single judge; procedure in benchmarking/evaluation/CODEX_JUDGE.md

scoring.split: framing 10, data 10, answer 20, mechanism 20, robustness 15, breadth 15, insight 10

anchors.0: Answers a different or vaguer question; no testable framing.
anchors.2: Operational definitions are given, but only one explanation is considered, or hypotheses are not tied to predictions.
anchors.4: Precise operational definitions; competing hypotheses with distinguishing predictions that structure the analysis.

anchors.0: Data mishandled (units, masks, grid, time or depth conventions) in a way that changes the results.
anchors.2: Correct handling, but the data's fitness for this question (model versus ocean, record length, resolution, missing variables) is not examined.
anchors.4: Correct handling, and fitness for this question is checked explicitly (for example against known observations or by internal consistency), with its consequences for the conclusions stated.

criteria.title: Quantitative answer against the answer key

anchors.0: Key quantities are missing, or wrong relative to the frozen answer key.
anchors.1: Quantities are reported, but most disagree with the answer key and no stated definition explains the difference.
anchors.2: About half of the answer-key items used by this criterion agree within tolerance (or differ only by a stated definition that the evaluator recomputed).
anchors.3: Most items agree within tolerance; one is missing or outside tolerance.
anchors.4: All answer-key items used by this criterion agree within tolerance, and their uncertainty is stated.

anchors.0: Description only, or process claims contradicted by independently computed reference diagnostics.
anchors.1: A biological or physical cause asserted from literature or intuition without a test in the supplied fields.
anchors.2: Departures from mixing are computed, but their cause is tested one way only; air-sea exchange, changing end-members or exchange between layers are not examined.
anchors.3: Carbon, phosphate and oxygen departures are compared quantitatively with a stated stoichiometry and agree with reference diagnostics; at least one alternative to biology is tested; unresolved parts are stated.
anchors.4: Competing causes (uptake and respiration of organic matter, air-sea exchange, changing end-members, transport between layers) are tested with quantitative diagnostics and uncertainty, consistent with independent references; the plume-to-bottom estimate states its assumptions; conclusions the data support are kept apart from unresolved alternatives; depth probes addressed. A justified finding that the data cannot separate two causes can receive full credit.

anchors.0: No sensitivity tests and no uncertainty.
anchors.2: One sensitivity test, or statistics that ignore short or autocorrelated records.
anchors.3: Several targeted sensitivity tests and suitable statistics; some key numbers lack uncertainty.
anchors.4: Targeted sensitivity tests on every choice that could change the conclusion (thresholds, baselines, regions, definitions), statistics suited to short and autocorrelated records, and uncertainty on all key numbers.

anchors.0: A single isolated diagnostic, with no link to related processes or published work.
anchors.1: Related processes or literature are mentioned but not used.
anchors.2: More than one variable or time scale is used, or results are compared with the literature, but mostly descriptively.
anchors.3: Processes or scales are connected and results are compared with published work with correct citations; one breadth probe is addressed well.
anchors.4: Scales and processes are connected (for example seasonal to interannual, physics to biogeochemistry), several variables are used coherently, agreement and disagreement with published work are stated with correct citations, and the breadth probes are addressed.

anchors.0: No clear answer to the question.
anchors.2: A clear answer, with generic limits and next steps.
anchors.4: A clear, quantified answer; precise limits of what the data can and cannot settle; specific next analyses or data that would settle the open points; at least one non-obvious insight supported by the analysis.

items.quantity: Surface departures from mixing per summer
items.procedure: On valid wet cells in 112-116 E, 20-23 N with water depth <=200 m, for June-August of each year 2011-2019: predict conservative TIC and PO4 with a three end-member mixing model on potential temperature and salinity (Pearl River plume water, offshore surface water, offshore subsurface water, each defined from the bound fields and recorded in spec.md). Report the departure (supplied minus predicted) in the surface plume (salinity below a stated threshold, 33.5 by default), its area-weighted mean, the area with a deficit and the ranking of the nine summers, in stated units.
items.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: sign of the mean departure exact; magnitude within 30% under matched end-members, or a difference explained by a stated end-member choice that the evaluator recomputed; Spearman of the yearly ranking at least 0.6)

items.procedure: With the same mixing model, departures of TIC, PO4 and oxygen in the bottom water (the deepest valid level, with the treatment of the level marked 9999 stated) on the same cells and summers: where and when the TIC and PO4 additions and the oxygen deficit are largest, their area-weighted means and the ranking of the nine summers.
items.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: sign exact; magnitude within 30% under matched end-members and bottom definition; Spearman at least 0.6; the largest addition in the same part of the shelf)

items.procedure: Regress TIC departures on PO4 departures and on oxygen departures, surface and bottom separately, and compare the slopes with organic-matter ratios (C:P about 106; oxygen to carbon about -1.3 in respiration). Report the part of the surface TIC deficit that phosphate does not match (air-sea exchange or another non-biological cause), which the supplied fields cannot confirm without pCO2 or a flux. Estimate the share of the bottom TIC addition that the surface deficit could supply over a stated residence time. Associations alone do not establish a dominant cause.
items.oracle: Independent reference diagnostics from the C_CORE and C_CARBON fields bound to this task
items.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: slopes within 25% of the reference or both consistent within uncertainty; the coupling share within a factor of two with its assumptions stated; alternative defensible analyses accepted)

depth_probes: Defines the three end-members from the supplied fields, checks that the mixing fractions stay between 0 and 1, and tests other defensible end-members and end-members that change between summers.
Separates the surface plume from the bottom water with a stated vertical criterion and treats the level marked 9999 explicitly.
Uses phosphate, which has no gas phase, to separate the biological part of the carbon departure from air-sea exchange, and oxygen as an independent check, without claiming a measured air-sea flux.
States how missing alkalinity, pCO2, nitrate, river loads and winds limit attribution; a departure from mixing is not a closed carbon budget.
breadth_probes: Compares surface deficits, bottom additions and their ratios with published Pearl River plume and shelf studies, distinguishing a nine-summer model record from single-summer cruise observations.
Links the carbon and phosphate signals to chlorophyll, stratification and bottom hypoxia on the same shelf.

literature_context.title: Dynamics of inorganic carbon and pH in a large subtropical continental shelf system: Interaction between eutrophication, hypoxia, and ocean acidification
literature_context.use: Summer observations in the Pearl River Estuary and on the adjacent shelf with multiple end-member mixing models: a DIC deficit of -191 +/- 54 umol/kg in the surface plume and an addition of about 139 +/- 21 umol/kg in the bottom hypoxic zone; a two-layer box model links at least 45 +/- 13% of the organic matter produced in the plume to 67 +/- 18% of the bottom DIC addition and oxygen consumption. Use it to judge the literature comparison only.

literature_context.title: Dynamics of the carbonate system in a large continental shelf system under the influence of both a river plume and coastal upwelling
literature_context.use: Northern South China Sea shelf in summer: mixing of plume water, offshore surface water and offshore subsurface water shapes DIC, with biological consumption visible in the plume and in coastal upwelling; a three end-member mixing model gives net community production of 36 +/- 19 (plume) and 23 +/- 26 (upwelled water) mmol C m-2 d-1. Use it to judge the literature comparison only.

literature_context.title: Nutrient dynamics and biological consumption in a large continental shelf system under the influence of both a river plume and coastal upwelling
literature_context.use: The same shelf in summer: a three end-member mixing model on potential temperature and salinity gives nutrient consumption as departures from conservative mixing; DIN:DIP consumption is 16.7 in the upwelling zone and the subsurface chlorophyll maximum and 61.3 +/- 8.7 in the plume. Use it to judge the literature comparison only.

literature_context.title: Tracing the origin of the oxygen-consuming organic matter in the hypoxic zone in a large eutrophic estuary: the lower reach of the Pearl River Estuary, China
literature_context.verification: Crossref metadata and the final abstract on the article page checked 2026-10-14
literature_context.use: July 2014, hypoxic zone of the lower Pearl River Estuary: a three end-member mixing model with the DIC mass balance and its carbon isotopes attributes about two thirds of the oxygen-consuming organic matter to marine production. Use it to judge the literature comparison only.

literature_context.title: Assessing ecosystem response to phosphorus and nitrogen limitation in the Pearl River plume using the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS)
literature_context.use: A ROMS nitrogen-phosphorus ecosystem model of the Pearl River plume: phosphorus limits production in the near and middle field and nitrogen in the far field; the N:P ratio falls from about 120 near the mouth to below 13.3 downstream. Use it to judge the literature comparison only.

gates: A number or citation that cannot be traced (to executed analysis, outputs or a real source) is unsupported; the criterion it supports scores at most 1, and a flag is recorded.
A different target (region, period or quantity) without justification: Q and M score at most 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except F at most 1.
